change: gRPC server TLS is required by default; plaintext requires explicit GRPC_ALLOW_INSECURE=true

acceptance.no_tls_or_missing_opt_in: server startup fails before database pool creation
acceptance.explicit_private_network_opt_in: plaintext server credentials are permitted only when GRPC_ALLOW_INSECURE=true
acceptance.invalid_opt_in: values other than true or false fail before database pool creation
acceptance.configured_tls: server uses TLS credentials when a certificate/key pair is configured

compose_policy.local_legacy_stack: explicitly configurable, defaults to enabled; host publication defaults to loopback
compose_policy.kernel_grpc_profile: explicitly enabled on the private kernel network with no host port

acceptance.kernel_profiles: removed incomplete agent-summary-worker service overrides from standard and runtime-role manifests; that service is not part of these Kernel profiles

verification.loopback_transport: ephemeral local listener tests were run with host access; no external endpoint was contacted
verification.compose_only: Compose contract tests render configuration with synthetic values; 37 Compose/profile checks passed and no container was started
verification.yaml_parse: passed for docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.prod.yml, and docker-compose.kernel-grpc.yml

limitations: No live remote gRPC endpoint or production certificate was tested.
The private-network opt-in remains a deployment trust decision; it does not provide encryption.
Tenant authorization, real runtime database roles, and REST policy parity remain open.
